findings.text: Mount scratch state keeps five pieces: a pid namespace reference plus a presence mask plus a hidepid level plus a gid number plus a pidonly selector for subset mode. It is allocated during context creation and released with its namespace reference on teardown.

Proc mount accepts four named options with distinct value kinds: gid as unsigned integer plus hidepid as string plus subset as string plus pidns as file or string, with a terminator entry. Central dispatch resolves names through a generic parser helper and records presence in the mask, while a small error helper reports invalid combinations.

Hidepid accepts either a numeric rendering checked against four allowed levels or one of four textual aliases for off and increasingly restrictive modes. Unrecognised numeric or textual input is rejected as invalid and leaves prior state unchanged.
Subset parsing splits the supplied value on commas, ignores empty segments, and accepts only the pid token which enables pidonly mode. Any other token fails the mount option processing.

Pidns selection accepts a file handed through configuration or a pathname opened read only, requires an nsfs object whose type is pid namespace, requires administrative capability in the target user namespace, and requires the target to be a descendant of the caller active namespace. Success replaces the context namespace and filesystem user namespace with new references.

Context lifecycle begins tied to the caller active pid namespace, continues through repeated option parsing, then either builds a fresh superblock or reconfigures a live one, and ends with teardown releasing namespace and credential references. Reconfiguration forbids subset change and pidns replacement while fresh creation allows both. The filesystem type carries the proc name with user namespace mount restrictions.

Resulting superblock carries private info with inherited namespace and credential and applied options, flags marking non executable and device free with directory time and setuid disabled, a small fixed block size with proc magic and one second granularity, maximal stacking depth to forbid stacking, disabled shrinker seeking, and installed root plus self links.

Boot initialization prepares pid link counts and self numbering, publishes a mounts alias under self, creates network and filesystem and driver and bus hierarchies with reserved mount points for nfsd and conditionally openprom, initializes tty and sys portions, and registers the filesystem type as the final step.

TTY portion creates a top directory and a line discipline directory preserved for userspace visibility, a driver directory limited to owner access because serial character counts could reveal secret length and timing, plus two sequence backed listings for disciplines and drivers.

Static root entry describes the top directory with a fixed low number and short name length and directory permissions open for reading and traversal, an initial link count of two and single reference, dedicated directory and inode operation tables, self parenting, empty child tree, and a canonical proc pathname.

Root lookup first attempts pid based resolution and falls back to generic handling, root directory iteration emits static entries until a process threshold then delegates to pid iteration, and attribute reporting uses a neutral identity mapping with link count augmented by live process count.

Per instance self and thread variants each present a named child under the root with a fresh inode using a preallocated number and symlink mode fully permissive owned by root, dedicated link resolution operations, and persistent pinning, with an error log on allocation failure.

Self link resolution reads the caller thread group identifier within the superblock pid namespace and reports missing when zero, otherwise renders the identifier in decimal into a freshly allocated short buffer using sleeping allocation when a dentry is present and atomic allocation otherwise, with automatic release after use. Number storage is immutable after boot.

Stat listing aggregates per possible processor time counters into a summary line and repeats per online processor lines with ten converted fields, reports total interrupt count plus dense per interrupt values with zero filling for gaps, then context switches and boot seconds adjusted for time namespace and fork and runnable and blocked counts, followed by total soft interrupt count and per type sums. Open sizing accounts for processor and interrupt counts.

Soft interrupt listing prints a header row with one column per possible processor then one row per type with fixed width per processor counters. Registration creates a permanent single shot entry under the top level.

Stat entry is registered at boot as permanent with custom open plus sequential read and seek and release handlers. Opening computes a buffer estimate and delegates to a sized single open helper that preallocates the sequential buffer and replaces the default after opening.

One build variant protects policy capture with task locking around retrieval and reference acquisition with a matching release that drops the reference, while an alternate build variant defines both capture and release as empty operations, indicating configuration dependent behaviour.

Maps locking context tracks an optional address space lock flag and an optional pinned area. Address space acquisition uses an interruptible read lock, clearing resets both trackers, area release ends area read protection, range entry takes read side protection and resets, and range exit prefers releasing the address space when held otherwise releases area plus read side protection. A second unlock variant releases the address space without touching the flag.
Two negative sentinel markers distinguish end and gate cases in area iteration, with end using negative one and gate using negative two.

Exact serial character counts risk inferring secret length and keystroke timing so driver visibility is restricted. Changing pidonly selection or pid namespace on a live remount is rejected to avoid inconsistent views and unsynchronised namespace access, with warnings guarding unexpected reconfigure paths.
Boot time interfaces publish the overall proc initialization plus tty setup plus self numbering helpers for early wiring.
Per instance interfaces expose installers for self and thread links plus the static root descriptor plus a sized single open helper for sequential files.
